documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Back at work since late January, adjusting. Baby is 3.5 months, doing fine per her.

Interval: placental abruption 10/13/23 with emergency C-section at 35 wks. Postpartum OB visit 11/28 unremarkable. Hgb 10.6 on 10/26.

HTN: home readings low 130s/80s. Labetalol 200 BID. Still on PNV and folic acid, plans to keep taking them for now.
Anxiety: busier, more worry about the baby than before, but sleeping when she can and functioning. GAD-7 7, PHQ-9 2. No meds wanted.

ROS otherwise negative.
Meds: labetalol 200 mg BID, PNV w/ DHA daily, folic acid 1 mg daily. Allergies: sulfa (rash), latex (contact dermatitis).
SH: former smoker, none since 2019. Alcohol rare.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. HEENT normal, thyroid normal. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, transverse C-section scar well healed. No edema. Skin normal. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
- Chronic HTN: at goal-ish on labetalol, continue. CMP.
- Anxiety: stable, no meds, revisit as needed.
- History of abruption: noted for any future pregnancy - early OB care.
- Recheck CBC.
- HM: Pap with HPV due 2026. Flu and COVID done in the fall.
RTC 6 months.

documents.body: Tessa - your hemoglobin has recovered fully, back to your usual 12. Kidney, liver and electrolytes are normal too. No changes. Have a good week.

documents.title: RE: Pregnant again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations. Yes, same plan: labetalol 200 mg twice daily, prenatal vitamin and folic acid. Good that OB is seeing you next week - make sure they know about the abruption and the C-section in October, though they'll have the records. Send me your home pressures if they start creeping up.

documents.title: Obstetrics Prenatal Update
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Dear Colleague,

Update on your patient Tessa Turcotte, now G2P1 at 19 weeks (LMP 04/09/2024, EDD 01/14/2025, consistent with first-trimester ultrasound).

Her history includes chronic hypertension on labetalol 200 mg twice daily and a placental abruption at 35 weeks in October 2023 delivered by emergency low transverse cesarean. Pressures have been well controlled this pregnancy. Prenatal labs are within normal limits.

After counseling she has chosen a trial of labor after cesarean, and we agree she is a candidate. We will plan delivery on our labor and delivery unit with a latex-free setup.

Allergies: sulfa (rash), latex (contact dermatitis).

Regards,
Obstetrics

documents.title: Obstetric and ICU Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received 01/15/2025)
Admitted 01/07/2025, discharged 01/14/2025.
Patient: Tessa Turcotte, 33 y/o, G2P2.

History: chronic hypertension on labetalol; anxiety disorder; placental abruption at 35 weeks in 10/2023 with emergency cesarean; laparoscopic appendectomy. Uneventful pregnancy this time with normal prenatal labs. Tdap given in our office 10/24/2024.
Allergies: sulfonamides (rash), latex (contact dermatitis).

Delivery: Admitted in spontaneous labor at term for a planned trial of labor after cesarean. Uncomplicated vaginal birth after cesarean on 01/07/2025; liveborn infant.

Event: Right after the placenta delivered she became acutely short of breath and visibly anxious. Started on supplemental oxygen and IV fluids, but she worsened: heart rate climbed quickly and she became hypotensive. She was intubated for respiratory distress and moved to the ICU. Within minutes she was oozing from IV sites and her gums. The uterus was firm and well contracted with no atony on pelvic exam, yet blood loss was soaking her perineal pads. Lungs with bilateral rales; skin cool and clammy.

Work-up: peripheral smear with schistocytes. Urine output fell and creatinine rose over the first day. Stat echo showed acute right ventricular dysfunction with normal LV function.

Diagnoses: amniotic fluid embolism; disseminated intravascular coagulation.

ICU course: supportive care with blood product replacement for the coagulopathy. Extubated 01/09. Bleeding stopped, coagulation studies normalized, urine output returned and creatinine came back to normal before transfer out of the ICU. Recovered on the postpartum floor and went home 01/14.

Discharge medications: labetalol 200 mg PO BID; prenatal vitamin with DHA daily; folic acid 1 mg daily.

Recommendations: repeat transthoracic echocardiogram in about 6 weeks to confirm RV recovery. PCP follow-up within 1-2 weeks with CBC, BMP and coagulation studies. Obstetric postpartum visit at 6 weeks.

reports.text: Indication: follow-up of acute right ventricular dysfunction during amniotic fluid embolism, 01/2025. Technically adequate study. Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness with normal systolic function. Normal diastolic function. Right ventricle normal in size with normal systolic function; TAPSE normal. Atria normal in size. Valves structurally normal without significant regurgitation or stenosis. Estimated RV systolic pressure normal. Inferior vena cava normal with normal respiratory variation. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Normal right ventricular size and systolic function. Normal left ventricular size and systolic function. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Maternal-Fetal Medicine Consultation
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
Dear Colleague,

We saw Ms. Turcotte on 07/22/2025 and again 08/12/2025, G3P2 at 10 weeks (LMP 06/03/2025, EDD 03/10/2026, confirmed by ultrasound).

Obstetric history: placental abruption at 35 weeks (10/2023) delivered by emergency cesarean; vaginal birth after cesarean at term (01/2025) complicated immediately after placental delivery by amniotic fluid embolism with DIC, ICU care and intubation, with a normal follow-up echocardiogram in 02/2025. Chronic hypertension on labetalol 200 mg twice daily, well controlled. Anxiety disorder.

We reviewed her history at length with her. Prenatal labs today are within normal limits. She continues labetalol, her prenatal vitamin with DHA and folic acid 1 mg. We will co-manage with her obstetric group with visits every 2-4 weeks and will plan her delivery at our center.

Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash); latex (contact dermatitis).

Sincerely,
Maternal-Fetal Medicine
